body: ## Description 🧘 Added Zen Mode toggle to documentation (`/docs`) pages: ### Features - Persistant - Like the theme toggle, the value of `'zen-mode'` gets saved in [localStorage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage) - That is so when a user closes their ethereum.org tab, or duplicates it, they can keep their settings and get back into flow when they return - Mobile friendly - The toggle doesn't show as an option, and is automatically turned off, when visited on mobile width screens ( < 1024px) since the mobile view of the docs is already pretty minimal - If a user shrinks a desktop-sized window to mobile-size with Zen Mode enabled, a more minimal UI may appear but nothing glitchy. Check out the screenshots below: - Shrunken window with zen-mode disabled: - - Shrunken window with zen-mode enabled: - - Modular - The Zen Mode toggle and its effects only appear in `/docs` pages - It shouldn't affect any other pages ### Demo (GIF) ![eth-org_zen-mode-demo](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/27740273/135869760-c1e729a7-61fb-49ed-8bbe-9e2a20aea126.gif) ### Lighthouse It doesn't affect the SEO or accessibility for the website, but it does slightly lower performance when it (Zen Mode) is enabled (as expected). #### `dev` branch score #### `zen-mode` branch score (with Zen Mode disabled) #### `zen-mode` branch score (with Zen Mode enabled) ## Related Issue #2737

Hi! Thanks for your great package!

I added minor mode for automatic running of `eslint-fix`.
Then we can write like:
```emacs-lisp
(eval-after-load 'js-mode
	   '(add-hook 'js-mode-hook #'eslint-fix-auto-mode))

(eval-after-load 'js2-mode
	   '(add-hook 'js2-mode-hook #'eslint-fix-auto-mode))
```

Note: Actually, `eval-after-load` is not needed because `add-hook` can handle undefined hook. So writing just like this is also valid:

(add-hook 'js-mode-hook #'eslint-fix-auto-mode)
(add-hook 'js2-mode-hook #'eslint-fix-auto-mode)

author: ghost
body:
This PR adds a `TauriPlugin` type in the Tauri plugin crate to unify plugins initialization styles.

Initially this change was attempting to make `TauriPlugin` own a `tauri::App<T>` that it could then pass to the runner function either directly or **via a non-send resource**, but sadly, this is simply impossible, due to two reasons:

- `tauri::App<tauri::Wry>` (which is the default type for Tauri apps) contains `tauri::Wry` which is `!Send + !Sync`. As `legion_ecs::Plugin` is `Send + Sync`, it is impossible to store an app inside the plugin [^1].
- While it possible to add the Tauri app to the world as a non-send resource, its `run(self)` method takes ownership of the instance and would force us to remove it from the resources before its first usage. This completely negates the benefit of making it a resource in the first place. Additionally, this would force us to make the resource a `Mutex<Option<tauri::App<T>>>` so we can "steal it" from the world, and feels really too complex for zero gain.

The chosen solution, was to allow callers to instanciate a `TauriPlugin` from a - possibly partially configured - `tauri::Builder<T>` instead. This provides the following interface:

```rust
    let builder = tauri::Builder::default();
    // Possibly some more operations done on the builder.

    App::new()
        .add_plugin(TauriPlugin::new_from_builder(
            builder,
            tauri::generate_context!(),
        ))
```

The method has to be provided with a `tauri::Context` which can only be instanciated from a Tauri-provided macro, that can only be called in the final binary. No factorization possible here either, as far as I understand.

[^1]: Putting it in an `Arc<Mutex<tauri::App<tauri::Wry>>>>` is not an option either, as `Mutex<T>` is only `Sync` if `T` is `Send`, and as we said, `tauri::App<tauri::Wry>` is `!Send`.

This PR updates [Flask](https://pypi.org/project/Flask) from **0.12.2** to **2.0.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.0.2
   ```
   -------------

Released 2021-10-04

-   Fix type annotation for ``teardown_*`` methods. :issue:`4093`
-   Fix type annotation for ``before_request`` and ``before_app_request``
    decorators. :issue:`4104`
-   Fixed the issue where typing requires template global
    decorators to accept functions with no arguments. :issue:`4098`
-   Support View and MethodView instances with async handlers. :issue:`4112`
-   Enhance typing of ``app.errorhandler`` decorator. :issue:`4095`
-   Fix registering a blueprint twice with differing names. :issue:`4124`
-   Fix the type of ``static_folder`` to accept ``pathlib.Path``.
    :issue:`4150`
-   ``jsonify`` handles ``decimal.Decimal`` by encoding to ``str``.
    :issue:`4157`
-   Correctly handle raising deferred errors in CLI lazy loading.
    :issue:`4096`
-   The CLI loader handles ``**kwargs`` in a ``create_app`` function.
    :issue:`4170`
-   Fix the order of ``before_request`` and other callbacks that trigger
    before the view returns. They are called from the app down to the
    closest nested blueprint. :issue:`4229`
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.0.1
   ```
   -------------

Released 2021-05-21

-   Re-add the ``filename`` parameter in ``send_from_directory``. The
    ``filename`` parameter has been renamed to ``path``, the old name
    is deprecated. :pr:`4019`
-   Mark top-level names as exported so type checking understands
    imports in user projects. :issue:`4024`
-   Fix type annotation for ``g`` and inform mypy that it is a namespace
    object that has arbitrary attributes. :issue:`4020`
-   Fix some types that weren't available in Python 3.6.0. :issue:`4040`
-   Improve typing for ``send_file``, ``send_from_directory``, and
    ``get_send_file_max_age``. :issue:`4044`, :pr:`4026`
-   Show an error when a blueprint name contains a dot. The ``.`` has
    special meaning, it is used to separate (nested) blueprint names and
    the endpoint name. :issue:`4041`
-   Combine URL prefixes when nesting blueprints that were created with
    a ``url_prefix`` value. :issue:`4037`
-   Roll back a change to the order that URL matching was done. The
    URL is again matched after the session is loaded, so the session is
    available in custom URL converters. :issue:`4053`
-   Re-add deprecated ``Config.from_json``, which was accidentally
    removed early. :issue:`4078`
-   Improve typing for some functions using ``Callable`` in their type
    signatures, focusing on decorator factories. :issue:`4060`
-   Nested blueprints are registered with their dotted name. This allows
    different blueprints with the same name to be nested at different
    locations. :issue:`4069`
-   ``register_blueprint`` takes a ``name`` option to change the
    (pre-dotted) name the blueprint is registered with. This allows the
    same blueprint to be registered multiple times with unique names for
    ``url_for``. Registering the same blueprint with the same name
    multiple times is deprecated. :issue:`1091`
-   Improve typing for ``stream_with_context``. :issue:`4052`
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.0.0
   ```
   -------------

Released 2021-05-11

-   Drop support for Python 2 and 3.5.
-   Bump minimum versions of other Pallets projects: Werkzeug >= 2,
    Jinja2 >= 3, MarkupSafe >= 2, ItsDangerous >= 2, Click >= 8. Be sure
    to check the change logs for each project. For better compatibility
    with other applications (e.g. Celery) that still require Click 7,
    there is no hard dependency on Click 8 yet, but using Click 7 will
    trigger a DeprecationWarning and Flask 2.1 will depend on Click 8.
-   JSON support no longer uses simplejson. To use another JSON module,
    override ``app.json_encoder`` and ``json_decoder``. :issue:`3555`
-   The ``encoding`` option to JSON functions is deprecated. :pr:`3562`
-   Passing ``script_info`` to app factory functions is deprecated. This
    was not portable outside the ``flask`` command. Use
    ``click.get_current_context().obj`` if it's needed. :issue:`3552`
-   The CLI shows better error messages when the app failed to load
    when looking up commands. :issue:`2741`
-   Add :meth:`sessions.SessionInterface.get_cookie_name` to allow
    setting the session cookie name dynamically. :pr:`3369`
-   Add :meth:`Config.from_file` to load config using arbitrary file
    loaders, such as ``toml.load`` or ``json.load``.
    :meth:`Config.from_json` is deprecated in favor of this. :pr:`3398`
-   The ``flask run`` command will only defer errors on reload. Errors
    present during the initial call will cause the server to exit with
    the traceback immediately. :issue:`3431`
-   :func:`send_file` raises a :exc:`ValueError` when passed an
    :mod:`io` object in text mode. Previously, it would respond with
    200 OK and an empty file. :issue:`3358`
-   When using ad-hoc certificates, check for the cryptography library
    instead of PyOpenSSL. :pr:`3492`
-   When specifying a factory function with ``FLASK_APP``, keyword
    argument can be passed. :issue:`3553`
-   When loading a ``.env`` or ``.flaskenv`` file, the current working
    directory is no longer changed to the location of the file.
    :pr:`3560`
-   When returning a ``(response, headers)`` tuple from a view, the
    headers replace rather than extend existing headers on the response.
    For example, this allows setting the ``Content-Type`` for
    ``jsonify()``. Use ``response.headers.extend()`` if extending is
    desired. :issue:`3628`
-   The ``Scaffold`` class provides a common API for the ``Flask`` and
    ``Blueprint`` classes. ``Blueprint`` information is stored in
    attributes just like ``Flask``, rather than opaque lambda functions.
    This is intended to improve consistency and maintainability.
    :issue:`3215`
-   Include ``samesite`` and ``secure`` options when removing the
    session cookie. :pr:`3726`
-   Support passing a ``pathlib.Path`` to ``static_folder``. :pr:`3579`
-   ``send_file`` and ``send_from_directory`` are wrappers around the
    implementations in ``werkzeug.utils``. :pr:`3828`
-   Some ``send_file`` parameters have been renamed, the old names are
    deprecated. ``attachment_filename`` is renamed to ``download_name``.
    ``cache_timeout`` is renamed to ``max_age``. ``add_etags`` is
    renamed to ``etag``. :pr:`3828, 3883`
-   ``send_file`` passes ``download_name`` even if
    ``as_attachment=False`` by using ``Content-Disposition: inline``.
    :pr:`3828`
-   ``send_file`` sets ``conditional=True`` and ``max_age=None`` by
    default. ``Cache-Control`` is set to ``no-cache`` if ``max_age`` is
    not set, otherwise ``public``. This tells browsers to validate
    conditional requests instead of using a timed cache. :pr:`3828`
-   ``helpers.safe_join`` is deprecated. Use
    ``werkzeug.utils.safe_join`` instead. :pr:`3828`
-   The request context does route matching before opening the session.
    This could allow a session interface to change behavior based on
    ``request.endpoint``. :issue:`3776`
-   Use Jinja's implementation of the ``|tojson`` filter. :issue:`3881`
-   Add route decorators for common HTTP methods. For example,
    ``app.post("/login")`` is a shortcut for
    ``app.route("/login", methods=["POST"])``. :pr:`3907`
-   Support async views, error handlers, before and after request, and
    teardown functions. :pr:`3412`
-   Support nesting blueprints. :issue:`593, 1548`, :pr:`3923`
-   Set the default encoding to "UTF-8" when loading ``.env`` and

-   ``flask shell`` sets up tab and history completion like the default
    ``python`` shell if ``readline`` is installed. :issue:`3941`
-   ``helpers.total_seconds()`` is deprecated. Use

We considered the following options for this:
- removing extra spaces in each form where primary/spouse legal names are updated
- removing extra spaces in a `before_save` hook on the model level (<- we went with this one)

author: myk002
body:
part of milestone 4 of #1842 

implements a new `#dig` blueprint for recording carved tracks, which were previously ignored by `blueprint`.

the `ecosystem` integration test harness is extended to decouple modes from phases (since now we have two phases that produce `#dig` blueprints) and track ecosystem tests are added.

This PR also does a bit of cleanup:
- the "all" prefix is removed from ecosystem tests, since they make the names too similar and was getting confusing
- the ecosystem test harness now configures `tiletypes` to properly clean up "empty" tiles -- previously `tiletypes` would restore all tiles to walls that still had a floor, but would not be able to determine the material for tiles that had been channeled out. Now we specify "stone" as the material for those tiles. We don't use "stone" for all tiles that we're restoring, though, since that would have a greater impact on the game map by removing all veins in the test area. We still lose the specific vein tiles that have been channeled out, but that is a much smaller area than the entire test area.

and fixes a bug in stockpile transcription: stockpiles without any categories enabled were being ignored. now we properly emit "c" for those stockpiles.

body:
https://artsyproduct.atlassian.net/browse/PLATFORM-3637
https://artsy.slack.com/archives/CP9P4KR35/p1633017320060100

[Ohm](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/artsy/ohm/946/workflows/a3f75999-0097-43d7-af60-8dc1e527e9b5/jobs/1467) and [Currents](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/artsy/currents/1493/workflows/ae61a4ca-735d-4169-9d02-67bc92b216c6/jobs/2202) builds are failing on nodesource due to [expired](https://letsencrypt.org/docs/dst-root-ca-x3-expiration-september-2021/) CA cert `DST Root CA X3`.

Tried bunch of potential work-arounds. This PR adopts [this workaround](https://github.com/nodesource/distributions/issues/1266#issuecomment-933228467) as it seems the only one that works across Debian versions.

Implement this for only two artsy images because the others are likely not affected or not really being used.

Tested builds locally (as there's no CI):

```
jian@artsy:~/code/docker-images/ruby/2.5.3-node-chrome$ docker run -it docker-images/ruby-2.5.3-node-chrome-me bash
root@9c345c2b19c6:/# node --version
v8.17.0

jian@artsy:~/code/docker-images/ruby/2.6.5-node-chrome$ docker run -it docker-images/ruby-2.6.5-node-chrome-me bash
root@cee363667562:/#
root@cee363667562:/# node --version
v10.24.1
```

author: dagood
body:
Adds a `dockerupdate` command alongside `dockerupdatepr`.

`dockerupdatepr` requires you to put your branch on a remote for the `-branch` flag, and runs Git operations in a temporary Git directory. This is not very useful when bringing up a whole new major.minor version of Go, because initial work is done locally, and it will likely be manually worked on and submitted as a dev PR.

`dockerupdate` works on an existing Git repo and doesn't run any Git commands, so it's easier to work with when developing nontrivial changes.

Both commands share `UpdateFlags`.
* For `SubmitUpdatePR`, `PRFlags` embeds `UpdateFlags`.
* For `RunUpdate`, `UpdateFlags` is used, plus one directory arg. (It doesn't seem worthwhile to create a command arg struct to contain the single `dockerupdate`-specific arg.)

body:
# Description
Upgrade our dependencies used in our API & Client to the latest major versions. The following outdated dependencies have been upgraded to their latest versions for API:

![Screenshot from 2021-10-04 13-52-37](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38117036/135914462-7700691c-fa9b-43e5-9b02-ef2a94f91eaa.png)

And for the client, partial dependencies have been upgraded (as some packages, including Bootstrap have introduced breaking changes):

![Screenshot from 2021-10-04 20-14-45](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38117036/135947099-0e004800-8b7a-4613-9060-93d4639e0c5d.png)

# Semver
Read about Semantic Versioning:  https://semver.org/ & https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v7/commands/npm-outdated
This is the important bit:
![Screenshot from 2021-10-04 14-59-25](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38117036/135916361-57c78932-0ed0-4768-b991-36525495003f.png)


# Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactoring
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Improvement

# Solution description

- We use `npm outdated` to list packages that have new versions
- Based on the screenshot in the description, we see a couple of packages that can be upgraded
- Based on Semantic Versions ([semver](https://semver.org/)), we see that a few of the packages can be upgraded safely with no breaking changes
- Those highlighted in red can be safely upgraded as they meet semver requirements, which are harmless minor/patch upgrades
- Those highlighted in yellow indicate that there's a version above semver requirements (new major versions, OR new `0.x` minor versions), and we need to upgrade these more carefully
- I paid special attention to `mongoose`'s v6 changelist and confirmed that the breaking changes introduced in `6.x` will not affect us: https://mongoosejs.com/docs/migrating_to_6.html. I did have to make a minor change to the way we connect to the DB though. 
- To upgrade the major versions and reflect the versions in the `package.json`, I used [`ncu`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/npm-check-updates)

# Implications

*Note that mongoose v6 will require **NODE.JS VERSION >= 12**, see [here](https://mongoosejs.com/docs/migrating_to_6.html#version-requirements) for more info.


# Tests

All unit tests pass? Y

Builds successfully? Y

Do all SA checks pass? Y



![Screenshot from 2021-10-04 14-27-03](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38117036/135914541-b886abe0-e051-4bd3-b792-77dd001d9052.png)
Now, there are no more outdated dependencies for the API.

The client still has outdated dependencies, but these carry significantly more risk to upgrade. I tried upgrading bootstrap but this broke our UI.

Provide steps in detail for reviewers to reproduce the expected result of the code changes.

Please verify that nothing is broken. 

# Risk
Medium as we're upgrading to major releases, which by definition, introduce breaking changes.

author: benhalpern
body: ## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable) - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Feature - [ ] Bug Fix - [ ] Optimization - [ ] Documentation Update ## Description This builds on https://github.com/forem/forem/pull/14857 to add a proper sitemap index to `robots.txt` and remove the way of doing things via `sitemap_generator` (✂️) which never fully supported all the contexts for Forem and abstracts away some logic which is more straightforward if we do without it. The old way of doing things was sending a big zip file to S3 in a way that is maybe technically accepted by Google, but not their preferred way, and was mostly broken across the Forem ecosystem. The zip/s3 way was entirely not supported via the Google Search Console. This new way standardizes our efforts around the most widely accepted sitemap practices. Basically, the sitemap we were serving in `robots.txt` was not really the way Google wants it and fully wasn't working in Forem Cloud or self-hosted Forems. This changes should be better for DEV as well as make this work properly for other Forems. This basically maintains the logic the current sitemap, and I think it is more or less appropriate. It orders posts by publish date, but tags and users more by total activity, as they are more of landing pages and "newness" isn't as much of a thing. We could revisit some of this. The underlying functionality is not yet documented in admin docs, so I could see giving this another pass before setting our documented logic in stone. ## Related Tickets & Documents https://github.com/forem/forem/pull/14857 ## QA Instructions, Screenshots, Recordings **Old:** **New:** Examine the logic and make sure everything basically makes sense. Check out this page to double-check that everything seems compatible: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/advanced/sitemaps/build-sitemap ### UI accessibility concerns? _If your PR includes UI changes, please replace this line with details on how accessibility is impacted and tested. author: felixguendling
body:
Enums need to be handled with care because the default size in bytes depends on the compiler implementation. Therefore, we decided that it's better to require manual implementation of serialization for enums.

However, it should be sufficient if the programmer confirms that it's a fixed sized enum he's trying to serialize. In this case, everything is fine. To reduce the effort of doing this, this PR introduces `is_fixed_size_enum(T)`. If this function returns true for `T = your_enum`, we assume that it's safe to (de)serialize this enum and enable support for this.

# Overview

This PR follows up from #8402 with an incremental refactor.

# Changelog

* For simplicity, instead of diffing the lists of loaded labware and loaded pipettes, subscribe to labware load and pipette load events, and map them 1:1. This is as discussed in https://github.com/Opentrons/opentrons/pull/8402#issuecomment-930559780.

## Code review

* Given our uncertainty about how to test this, is it worth adding `LegacyContextPlugin` unit tests for labware loads and pipette loads, right now?

## Smoke test plan

Upload and run PAPIv2 or JSON Schema v4 or lower protocols, and verify:

* Commands are still mapped to naive `commandType: custom` wrappers
* Labware and pipette loads are still reflected
    * Labware and pipette loads should now be in the same order as they appeared in the protocol

# Risk assessment

No risk to production code *yet,* since this is behind a feature flag.

Some risk that this will break what was implemented in #8402.

body: ### Description - Creates a ErrorFallback component - Adds error boundary with ErrorFallback to catch any JS exception and allows the user to restart the app - Adds an ErrorFallbackScreen so we can conditionally navigate to the screen in case of an error with webSocket - Enables option to fetch on background on iOS to see if it helps when app is inactive to keep the connection alive - Add a new condition to create a new socket, in case it's disconnected. - Clean up some unused ios references . - Handles error on gnosis fetch fails - Handles error on sendDepot, because if the converter or safes call fails it means the ws is probably with some problems, and without them we can't actually send anything. - [x] Completes #(CS-2041) ### Checklist - [x] All UI changes have been tested on a small device ### Screenshots // Websocket error > // General error

author: tmeschter
body:
Fixes [AB#1412179](https://devdiv.visualstudio.com/0bdbc590-a062-4c3f-b0f6-9383f67865ee/_workitems/edit/1412179).

It is possible to run into a deadlock if you start a project with Hot Reload turned on, exit the process, and then quickly start the project again. On a thread pool thread we'll be processing the `Exit` event for the process, and have entered the semaphore that protects our internal Hot Reload state (in `ProjectHotReloadSessionManager`). We then try to write a message to the Output Windows which requires a transition to the UI thread. Meanwhile, on the UI thread we trying to create a new Hot Reload session for the second project start, but to do that we need to enter the semaphore. And there's the deadlock: the main thread is blocked waiting for the semaphore, but the semaphore can't be released until code runs on the main thread.

Note that we're following the VS threading rules and I had expected that to prevent this sort of issue (for example, by allowing the main thread to pump messages while waiting to enter the semaphore) but perhaps it isn't enough. Regardless, we can solve this ourselves.

One option would be to avoid outputting any messages while the semaphore is held. However, this would be difficult to enforce and would make the code more complex as we would need to separate generating the message from actually outputting the message in several places.

Instead, this change recognizes that when we output a message we don't actually care if it is output right away or at some later time, so long as that later time isn't too far in the future. The messages we output are strictly for the benefit of the user, not for the correct operation of Hot Reload. As such we can replace the awaitable `IHotReloadDiagnosticOutputService.WriteLineAsync` with the fire-and-forget `IHotReloadDiagnosticOutputService.WriteLine`. We can still write output where it is convenient for us to do so, but we will no longer delay releasing the semaphore in order to do so.

While I was at it, I replaced the use of `IVsOutputWindowPane.OutputString` with the `IVsOutputWindowPaneExtensions.OutputStringNoPump` extension method. This calls the preferred forms `IVsOutputWindowPaneNoPump.OutputStringNoPump` or `IVsOutputWindowPane.OutputStringThreadSafe`, as available.

author: iuliana-prodan
body:
Here's a summary of this pull request:

1. Compared to other supported codecs, like MP3 or AAC, SRC has:
- a different flow for `.init_process` and `.process` operations;
- operates on samples, rather than bytes;
To fix the above differences I had to add new operations specific for the SRC codec from Xtensa.

2. Now, in codec adapter component we only update the frame format of the buffer parameters.
For SRC we need to update also the rate with the pipeline one, otherwise DAI throws an error because PCM rate parameter does not match hardware DAI rate parameter set during dai_set_config();

3. For SRC I added a simplified version of `.copy` function of codec adapter component.
- we don't need a `local_buffer` or `deep_buff_bytes` since we can send the data directly to the codec to process it;
- also, `bytes_to_process` must be computed based on the codec input and output buffer sizes, the available data in the source buffer and the free bytes in the sink buffer.

4. For now, input and output rates are hardcoded in topology, in control bytes from Codec Adapter component.

Using all the above one is now capable of converting the support rates from Xtensa SRC {8000, 11025, 12000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100, 48000, 64000, 88200, 96000, 128000, 176400, 192000} Hz. to 48000 Hz.
I only tested S16, but Xtensa SRC supports also S24.

This pull request should be used on top of #4841

body:
1. Adds `historical_mississippi_records_scraper` for data from the Mississippi DOC for cases, deaths, vaccines. 
2. Adds `historical_tx_vaccine_records_scraper` for vaccine data from TDCJ. Also gives us updated population values for staff and incarcerated people! 
3. Makes the manual Mississippi scraper defunct (since we want the facility-level data), and I renamed the manual Google Sheet so we don't accidentally pull from it. 

Note – I set these up as historical scrapers so that we can assign the date to not today. We also don't want them to run in the main set since we only want to run them when we get updated records. I synced the raw files (not the extracted ones yet though) so you have them ([here](http://104.131.72.50:3838/scraper_data/raw_files/2021-09-03_historical_mississippi_records.csv) for Mississippi and [here](http://104.131.72.50:3838/scraper_data/raw_files/2021-09-16_historical_texas_vaccine_records.pdf) for Texas). 

**IMPORTANT** – need to update the anchored values for Texas to match this data (23,345 for staff and 97,029 for incarcerated people) before merging this PR. It's not at all clear to me why these denominators are so much lower than they should be though. I'm on the fence about what to do about the Mississippi population values though (i.e. whether to update the anchor to reflect the denominator needed to match the percentage in this file or not). 

There will also almost certainly be some new spellings to add to the crosswalks.

author: thatoddmailbox
body:
Both FileServer and NewFileTransport can try to seek a file, specifically
when MIME type sniffing is performed. This can be somewhat surprising to an
implementer of an fs.FS, as their filesystem will appear to work until a
user tries to access a file with an unrecognized extension (which requires
type sniffing and therefore seeking). With FileServer, this results in a
"seeker can't seek" message, which is not very clear for the developer.

The issue arises because fs.FS does not require Seek, while http.FileSystem
does. Therefore, this change adds a line to the documentation of net/http's
adapter function mentioning the requirement.

# Partial workflow

Remember the [custom workflow](https://github.com/jeff-try-code/github-actions-for-ci/issues/4) we are attempting to create for the team? Here's our status on the list of requirements we defined:

- :white_check_mark: **test against multiple targets** so that we know if our supported operating systems and Node.js versions are working
- :white_check_mark: **dedicated test job** so that we can separate out build from test details
- :white_check_mark: **access to build artifacts** so that we can deploy them to a target environment
- **branch protections** so that the `main` branch can't be deleted or inadvertently broken
- **required reviews** so that any pull requests are double checked by teammates
- **obvious approvals** so we can merge quickly and potentially automate merges and deployments

The last three remaining items don't really belong in a `code, build, and test` pipeline because they have to do with processes that involve humans.

## Step 14: Automate the review process

GitHub Actions can run multiple workflows for different event triggers. Let's create a new approval workflow that'll work together with our Node.js workflow.

### :keyboard: Activity: Add a new workflow file to automate the team's review process

1. Create a [new file](https://github.com/jeff-try-code/github-actions-for-ci/new/team-workflow/?filename=.github/workflows/approval-workflow.yml), `.github/workflows/approval-workflow.yml`, on this branch
1. Enter a name for your workflow in the new file, something like:
    ```yaml
    name: Team awesome's approval workflow
    ```

I'll respond when you commit to this branch.
